units.why: "must complete a UNCG ITS Pre-Purchase Software and Hardware Review" is institutional review of AI tools before purchase: P65.

units.passage: As with any software purchase, submit procurement requests via Jaggaer regardless of the dollar value. If you have already purchased a generative AI tool, please let UIT know.

units.passage: As with any software purchase, submit a non-standard procurement request via Jaggaer regardless of the dollar value when using sensitive data.

units.passage: completing the AI Review Committee Review Process if applicable (see the AI Review Committee FAQ for further details

units.passage: Any use of an AI detection tool requires prior approval of the tool by the AI Review Committee, given the issues with accuracy and because it may involve sensitive personal information or impact the legal rights of students
units.why: "Any use of an AI detection tool requires prior approval of the tool by the AI Review Committee" lets detectors be used only after approval, which is P65 (review and approve tools) rather than P39 since use is still possible.
units.fit_note: Applies to detectors specifically and ties approval to accuracy, sensitive data and student legal rights.

units.passage: If the use of an AI system involves inputting any confidential information, personal information, or restricted research data (see the AI Policy for definitions), or could impact the legal rights or safety of any individual, instructors must submit the use of the AI tool for review by the AI Review Committee.
units.why: "instructors must submit the use of the AI tool for review by the AI Review Committee" when confidential data are input or rights could be affected; review of AI tool use, P65.

units.passage: Similarly, do not use third-party AI tools such as meeting recorders, note-taking tools, and writing proofreaders unless the tool has been approved by the AI Review Committee and the Office of Information Security. Third-party AI tools can use this data to train their model, as d escribed in Item #1 above
units.why: "do not use third-party AI tools such as meeting recorders, note-taking tools, and writing proofreaders unless the tool has been approved" requires approval of such tools; P65.

units.passage: Do not sign a contract with a vendor that offers AI services or incorporates AI features and functions into its services without first following the Office of Information Security vendor review process as well as the AI Review Committee process (if applicable)
units.why: "Do not sign a contract with a vendor that offers AI services ... without first following the ... vendor review process" requires vendor review, P65.

units.passage: Questions about AI usage pertaining to information security, privacy considerations, use of AI tools with Level 2 or above data, or evaluation of new third-party AI products can be directed to the Northwestern IT Information Security Office .
units.why: This routes questions on security, privacy, Level 2 or above data and 'evaluation of new third-party AI products' to the Information Security Office. The review of third-party AI products is closest to P65 (vendor review), though no vendor rule is stated.
units.fit_note: Names the office that evaluates new third-party AI products and handles Level 2+ data questions; no limit on sharing data with vendors is stated.

units.policy: All third-party AI tools must comply with applicable data privacy laws (e.g., FERPA, HIPAA, GDPR), and procurement must verify vendor compliance.
units.why: The sentence "All third-party AI tools must comply with applicable data privacy laws ... and procurement must verify vendor compliance" is one source sentence; A anchored only the procurement half. B's fuller anchor and policy are kept, both coders gave P65.

units.passage: The university has a rigorous review process for AI technology ( Software, Applications, and Website Purchasing Checklist Request), ensuring all AI tools undergo thorough evaluation by cross-functional experts before implementation.
units.why: "The university has a rigorous review process ... ensuring all AI tools undergo thorough evaluation" describes the existing process rather than commanding anyone (A informs, B must). Final informs/neutral.

units.passage: All approved AI systems are subject to re-evaluation upon major updates or model changes.
units.why: "All approved AI systems are subject to re-evaluation upon major updates or model changes" sets a requirement on approved tools (A informs, B must), but it is a procedure, not a stance on AI use. Final must/neutral.
units.fit_note: Adds periodic re-evaluation of already approved tools.

units.passage: shall establish a standardized and transparent approval process for the acquisition, development, and/or deployment of AI technologies. The approval process requires the thorough review and ratification of AI technology by designated authorities in consultation with Procurement Services, Information Technology Services, and other relevant University departments to ensure compliance with University AI policy.
units.why: Procedure 1 requires 'a standardized and transparent approval process for the acquisition, development, and/or deployment of AI technologies', vetting of tools (P65 covers vendor review; this is the approval process).
units.fit_note: Approval of AI technologies before acquisition or deployment, not only vendor contracts. / Approval process for any AI technology acquired, built or deployed, not only vendor agreements.

units.passage: Implement measures to assess and mitigate risks associated with third -party AI vendors, including vendor selection, data sharing agreements, contractual obligations, assessing vendor reliability, data security practices, adhering to ethical standards, by consulting with Procurement Services, and undergoing the University’s software decision analysis process.
units.why: 'assess and mitigate risks associated with third-party AI vendors' including data sharing agreements is vendor review (P65).

units.passage: Contracts with AI vendors should include provisions for data protection, privacy safeguards, in addition to clauses for non -compliance and dispute resolution by consulting with Procurement Services and following the software decision analysis process to ensure compliance.
units.why: Contracts 'should include provisions for data protection, privacy safeguards' and non-compliance clauses; vendor agreement content (P65).

units.passage: Conduct regular audits and assessments in collaboration with ITS to monitor the performance and security of third-party AI solutions.
units.why: 'Conduct regular audits and assessments' of third-party AI solutions' performance and security is monitoring of vendors (P65).
units.fit_note: Ongoing audits of third-party AI performance and security, beyond contract review.

units.passage: users of AI should avoid sharing personal or sensitive data with the tool and should not input moderate or high-risk Penn data as defined by the Penn Data Risk Classification , or intellectual property, without: Careful consideration and understanding of the tool’s use of Penn data and the service provider’s stated rights to the data, including, but not limited to whether the service provider offers the option to opt-out of using customer’s data to train the AI; A contract in place to protect Penn data; and Review by Penn’s Privacy Office and consultation with the Office of Information Security as coordinated by Procurement when moderate or high-risk data is involved. Consultation with the Penn Center for Innovation, where intellectual property is involved.
units.policy: Users should not input moderate or high-risk Penn data or intellectual property into an AI tool without careful consideration of the tool's use of Penn data, a contract in place to protect Penn data, and review by Penn's Privacy Office with consultation with the Office of Information Security (coordinated by Procurement); where intellectual property is involved, consultation with the Penn Center for Innovation.
units.why: The privacy list opens "should not input moderate or high-risk Penn data ... or intellectual property, without" careful consideration, "A contract in place to protect Penn data" and Privacy Office review. It binds all users during use of an AI tool and restricts input unless the listed conditions are met, so it is a restrict rule coded P65 (review and approve tools, vendors and data sharing).
